question.prompt: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target. You may assume each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.
expectedPoints: Clarify constraints (negative numbers, array size, memory constraints)
Suggest linear time approach using a Hash Map tracking complement
Analyze O(N) time complexity and O(N) auxiliary space complexity
Handle edge cases like duplicate values that sum to target
Provide unit test cases (e.g., negative numbers, minimum array length)
commonMistakes: Defaulting to O(N^2) brute force nested loops without optimization
Using the same element index twice

transcript: Candidate: Uh, okay. Two sum. I guess I will just loop through the array twice with two for loops, like for i from 0 to n and for j from 0 to n. If nums[i] plus nums[j] equals target, I return [i, j]. That should work for everything, right? Interviewer: What happens if target is 6 and nums[0] is 3? Candidate: Oh, it might return [0, 0]. I can just check if i is not equal to j. Complexity? I don't know, it's just two loops so maybe O(N) or O(N squared)? I don't think we need a hash table, nested loops are simpler. No tests needed.
notes: Brute force O(N^2), failed to prevent duplicate index until prompted, dismissive of tests and hash map optimization.
